item.title: Dolly Parton’s sister, Stella says machine changed her vote to Republican
item.description:
Over the past few days, a number of voters, including Dolly Parton's sister, Stella Parton, have taken to social media to report problems with voting machines, saying the devices did not display their desired candidate or changed their selections. The reported complications come after hundreds of thousands of Tennesseans started casting ballots on Oct. 14 for governor, U.S. Congress, the Tennessee General Assembly and three proposed constitutional amendments.
Social media users have reported needing multiple attempts to cast ballots for their preferred candidates because of alleged issues with electronic voting machines. Stella Parton took to Facebook on Oct. 21 and encouraged voters to check their ballots after she said it took her three attempts to select her preferred candidate. "Again, I remind you to double check your ballot before you print it out and put it through the machine," wrote Parton. "I finally called over a poll worker when my ballot kept flipping to the wrong candidate on the third try. No, this is not a joke! But what good is your vote if the machines are ‘fixed’ this is the issue here." "So, this happened to me when I early voted the other day… at the time I just attributed it to fat finger syndrome, but I have seen more and more people in Tennessee saying this has happened to them too," another Facebook user added.
Following her initial post, Parton shared a separate Facebook post, urging voters to hit the polls despite the issue. "In Tennessee last week at the Hermitage Library where I voted, I had to go back three times and correct my vote because it kept defaulting to Marsha Blackburn. I would never vote for her for anything. "I’m putting this out here because when we vote, we take it seriously but we try not to hold up the long lines. Do it anyway. Don’t let them rig this election." Similar claims have also appeared on X. "There is a very disturbing trend being seen in early voting. Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Ohio are reporting difficulties getting the machines to accept democratic votes. The machines change them back to Republican unless the voter persists, pressing several times to get the correct vote to go through," an X user wrote. How the Tennessee Secretary of State's office says voters should check their ballots "Tennessee's voting systems are designed with multiple safeguards to help ensure that ballots are recorded consistent with voter intent," Tennessee Coordinator of Elections Mark Goins told The Tennessean regarding the reported issues. In addition to assuring voters that Tennessee's voting system has multiple safeguards, Goins reminded voters of the several opportunities they have to verify their selections before casting a ballot, including the selection screen, review screen and paper record. What to do if you encounter issues at the polls If voters encounter problems at the polls like the ones mentioned, they should immediately notify a poll worker or their local county election commission so the issue can be addressed before the ballot is cast. Tennessee election officials also encourage voters to carefully review their ballot selections before final submission. The Tennessee Secretary of State provides election resources and contact information on their website. https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/10/22/dolly-parton-sister-tennessee-vote-changed-republican/92382903007/

item.title: RESIGNATION IS NOT FUCKING ACCOUNTABILITY.
item.description:
A one-year-old child is dead. Kohen Wiley was killed when Senatobia police officer Hunter Foster fired three shots during a confrontation in a Walmart parking lot.
Now, following the release of body-camera footage, Foster has resigned. And that's supposed to be where the story ends? A badge isn't a shield from accountability. A resignation isn't a verdict. And handing in your uniform doesn't answer the questions a grieving family deserves to have answered. If the shooting was justified, let the evidence withstand independent scrutiny. If laws were broken, prosecute accordingly. Because a child doesn't get to come home simply because an officer no longer reports for duty. Kohen Wiley deserved a future. His family deserves answers. #JusticeForKohenWiley #PoliceAccountability #JusticeForKohen #Transparency #Accountability #StreetArt #StencilArt #PoliticalStreetArt #ArtAsProtest #ProtestArt #Artivism #VisualSatire #SocialCommentary #ArtWithAMessage
